name: Wisp
tagline: Desktop air quality & hazardous gas sentinel
summary: Monitors ambient air quality, hazardous gases (CO, smoke, VOCs), temperature, and humidity using an ESP32 with an MQ-135 sensor and DHT22 probe, alerting with an audible piezo buzzer and displaying live AQI telemetry on a 0.96" OLED.

parts.name: ESP32 NodeMCU DevKit V1
parts.why: Dual-core processor with onboard ADC and 2.4GHz WiFi for IoT telemetry streaming

parts.name: MQ-135 Hazardous Gas & Air Quality Sensor
parts.why: Detects ammonia, nitrogen oxides, smoke, benzene, and CO2 in ambient air

parts.name: DHT22 / AM2302 Precision Temperature & Humidity Sensor
parts.why: Accurately measures ambient room temperature and relative humidity with 0.5°C precision

parts.name: 0.96 inch I2C OLED Display (SSD1306)
parts.why: Renders real-time AQI gauge, temperature, humidity, and safety status

parts.name: Active Piezo Buzzer 5V
parts.why: Sounds an urgent 85dB acoustic pulse alarm if hazardous gas concentrations exceed safety limits

parts.name: Single 18650 Li-ion Battery Holder
parts.why: Enables cordless portable operation for roaming room air quality sweeps

product.pageHeadline: Wisp — Clean air intelligence for your workspace and home.
bullets: Simultaneous dual-sensor tracking: hazardous gases (MQ-135) plus precision temperature & humidity (DHT22)
ESP32 dual-core IoT engine ready for local OLED display or Home Assistant WiFi MQTT integration
85 dB active acoustic buzzer provides instant early warning before toxic VOCs or smoke accumulate
Vented geometric chassis engineered with targeted airflow chimneys over thermal sensing elements
Under ₹1,200 bill of materials using readily available maker electronics

buildSteps: Step 1: 3D print the vented Wisp enclosure base and snap-fit lid using PLA or PETG with 20% infill.
Step 2: Press the ESP32 DevKit into the inner retention clips with the Micro-USB port aligned to the side cutout.
Step 3: Insert the MQ-135 sensor module into the right ventilation chamber to allow natural convection over the sensing element.
Step 4: Mount the DHT22 temperature and humidity sensor into the bottom intake bracket away from the heated MQ-135.
Step 5: Snap the SSD1306 OLED display into the lid window and connect I2C wiring (SDA to D21, SCL to D22).
Step 6: Solder or wire the active piezo buzzer to pin D18 with ground return to the common rail.
Step 7: Connect 5V USB power, let the MQ-135 preheat for 3 minutes, and observe real-time ambient air quality metrics.

agentLog.detail: Parsed request: Desktop air quality and hazardous gas sentinel with display and alarm.
Selected ESP32, MQ-135, DHT22, SSD1306 OLED, and 5V Buzzer. Total BOM: ₹1,165.
Configured D34 (ADC1) for gas sensor, D4 for 1-wire DHT22, D18 for acoustic buzzer, and D21/D22 for I2C OLED.
Generated sketch.ino with floating calibration filter and triple-pulse acoustic siren.
Compiled target esp32:esp32:esp32 successfully (flash: 242 KB, RAM: 18 KB, 0 errors).
Simulated ADC surge: verified serial triggers BUZZER_ACTIVE upon exceeding 1200 raw ADC.
Generated OpenSCAD enclosure (115 x 85 x 40 mm) featuring dual convection airflow chimneys.
Thermal separation clearance check passed: 42 mm isolation between heated MQ-135 and DHT22.
